title: Inseego M2100 port:  full code released today (touchscreen UI, Home Assistant add-on, Meshtastic alerts)
body:
### What would you like to share?

Just thought I'd make a quick post that we released the full code to the M2100 port + Home Assistant Add-on analyzer / alert with Meshtastic + a custom touchscreen UI for the M2100 at https://github.com/mallorybowes/rayhunter/tree/m2100-support.  The build series is documented at https://tpc.institute/projects/rayhunter-m2100 which describes the port, the HA integration, the device profiles, the Meshtastic integration, and the standalone fixed Sentinel that will most likely turn any stock Rayhunter device into a fixed sensor that learns your neighborhood and alerts with or without Home Assistant.  (Code for a standalone version of the Sentinel will be released soon as we're still developing that branch.)

Of note in the build, please be aware that it requires third-party firmware that is hosted on XDA.  (As documented in the build series, we tried the best we could to find a way in on the stock firmware and we weren't successful.)  There were 5 issues we had to solve to get things working that I feel would be of some value to the upstream project:

<details>
<summary>1. the 24-byte diag ioctl struct (msm-4.14)</summary> 

https://github.com/mallorybowes/rayhunter/commit/5dbd333

Solves: DIAG_IOCTL_SWITCH_LOGGING fails (EFAULT, then EINVAL); no capture. Likely affects other 4.14-era Qualcomm devices, not just the M2100, and confirmed the fix worked in our Pixel 4 XL port.

</details>

<details>
<summary>2. stripping the 8-byte multi-radio header before parsing</summary> 

https://github.com/mallorybowes/rayhunter/commit/6a4b0c6

Solves: every message fails as “ID 408 not found on ResponsePayload” (the 0x98 tag is read as a Response opcode). Affects modems that send it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>3. keeping log versions the parser doesn't know (0xb114, 0xb063)</summary> 

https://github.com/mallorybowes/rayhunter/commit/aa04b06 

Solves: 0xb114 v161 and MAC DL v49 fail the version == 1 assert; 29,577 of 29,658 skipped messages in a 16-hour capture; the skip log reached 186 MB and filled rootfs. No analyser uses those logs, so detection was never affected.

</details>

<details>
<summary>4. bounded parse-error logging (the fix-parse-error-log-volume branch)</summary> 

https://github.com/mallorybowes/rayhunter/commit/4a094bc

Solves: each parse error logged the whole payload; run.log reached 334 MB on a 236 MB rootfs, recording died silently, the web UI kept looking normal. The most generally useful of the five: any device can hit it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>5. zero-padding short diag structs (the diag-zero-pad branch).</summary> 

https://github.com/mallorybowes/rayhunter/commit/9f85107 + https://github.com/mallorybowes/rayhunter/commit/9b0da46 

Solves: the ioctl carries no length, so the short 12/20-byte attempts handed the driver stack junk; on a Pixel 4 XL that left the driver in a state where every request was refused. Looked like boot timing. Also: the diag task’s setup error was swallowed, so the daemon served its page with /dev/diag closed.

</details>

I'm a security researcher and the code was written by Claude which is why I'm not going to create upstream PRs for these fixes.  But if someone does decide to take a look and vouch for the code, I'd appreciate a co-author credit.  

The first three have already come in handy as I used those to port a Pixel 4 XL and currently have Rayhunter + a Pixel-centric Sentinel port running on it.  (Code to follow soon.)

Big shout out to @untitaker, @cooperq, and @lukejenkins for helping me with various parts of the build series!

### Prerequisites

- [X] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/EFForg/rayhunter/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [X] No generative AI (including LLMs) tools were used to write this post.
